question: Should ClawHub continue owning support for the legacy `molt.bot` installer failure, or treat that path as retired/redirected to the current OpenClaw installer and ClawHub install guidance?
rationale: The observable failure is in a hosted legacy installer whose source is absent from current ClawHub main, so automation cannot choose between hardening, redirecting, or retiring that path without maintainer intent.

options.title: Retire or redirect legacy installer
options.body: Treat `molt.bot` as a legacy alias and resolve this by pointing users to supported OpenClaw/ClawHub install commands with a clear Node support range.

options.title: Own and harden the installer
options.body: Bring the hosted installer source under a traceable owner and fix the unmatched cleanup glob and macOS/Homebrew Node compatibility path.

options.title: Wait for fresh reproduction
options.body: Keep the issue waiting on the reporter until they confirm the failure still occurs with the current hosted installer or supported install commands.

recommendation.title: Retire or redirect legacy installer
recommendation.body: Treat `molt.bot` as a legacy alias and resolve this by pointing users to supported OpenClaw/ClawHub install commands with a clear Node support range.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is the strongest available routing candidate from current CLI/package and docs history.
